# OpenGlass UI

> The open-source Liquid Glass UI system for React and the web. Forty accessible native-DOM components, neutral adaptive themes, CSS-first glass, opt-in SVG/SDF refraction and opt-in WebGL2 for media you own.

Published on npm as `open-glass-ui` (MIT, zero runtime dependencies, React 18 or newer as a peer). Source: https://github.com/moekoelueker/open-glass-ui. Live demo: https://moelueker.com/liquid-glass.

Read the full reference first. It lists every component with its required props and exact callback names, and it ships in the package at `node_modules/open-glass-ui/llms-full.txt`:

- [Full consumer reference (llms-full.txt)](https://github.com/moekoelueker/open-glass-ui/blob/main/llms-full.txt)

## Minimal setup

```tsx
import "open-glass-ui/styles.css";
import { Button, GlassSystemProvider, Tabs } from "open-glass-ui";

export function App() {
  return (
    <GlassSystemProvider>
      <Tabs
        label="Sections"
        items={[
          { value: "one", label: "One", content: <Button variant="primary">Continue</Button> },
          { value: "two", label: "Two", content: <p>Second panel</p> },
        ]}
      />
    </GlassSystemProvider>
  );
}
```

## Entry points

- `open-glass-ui`: `GlassSystemProvider` (runtime, theme and toast queue in one), `Glass`, hooks, forty recipes, theme and material utilities, public types.
- `open-glass-ui/styles.css`: import once. With Tailwind CSS v4, import it into a cascade layer (see the reference).
- `open-glass-ui/core`: server-safe geometry, material and theme helpers; no React.
- `open-glass-ui/webgl`: opt-in WebGL2 surface for an owned image, canvas or video.
- Never import `@open-glass-ui/*`; those workspace packages are private and not on npm.

## Rules that prevent most errors

- Callback names differ per component. Slider, TextField, Textarea, Select and Checkbox use native `onChange`; Switch uses `onCheckedChange`; SegmentedControl, Tabs, RadioGroup, SearchField and NumberField use `onValueChange`. The table is in the reference.
- Required shapes: `Tabs` takes `items=[{ value, label, content }]`, `Menu` and `Popover` take `trigger`, `Select` takes `options=[{ value, label }]`.
- `useToast()` returns `{ toast, dismiss }` and works below `GlassSystemProvider`.
- Card, Toolbar, Dock, Dialog, Drawer, Menu and Popover already paint glass; do not wrap them in `Glass`.
- The provider writes `--ogui-*` tokens inline, so override them through its `theme` prop, its `style`, or a descendant class, not on `:root`.
- Recipes inherit the app font; set one on `body`.
- `renderer="auto"` is CSS-first. SDF refraction goes on a decorative aria-hidden layer, never on a `Glass` that holds text. WebGL is only for owned media.
- `design="liquid"` is the default look; `design="classic"` restores the 0.3 look. Scopes nest and the nearest wins.
- Keep text, controls and semantics in the DOM. Reduced motion, reduced transparency and forced colors are designed states.
- In Next.js App Router, put providers and hook-using components behind `"use client"`.

Working on the repository itself: start with [docs/handoff/CURRENT.md](https://github.com/moekoelueker/open-glass-ui/blob/main/docs/handoff/CURRENT.md), then [HANDOVER.md](https://github.com/moekoelueker/open-glass-ui/blob/main/docs/handoff/HANDOVER.md) and the [context pack](https://github.com/moekoelueker/open-glass-ui/blob/main/context/README.md).
